company.name: Taskhive
company.description: Project management for agencies: tasks, timelines and client portals. Agencies pay per seat on the Business plan.

title: Taskhive: a month of feedback
brief: Taskhive's inbox for the last 30 days holds 62 pieces of feedback: app reviews, support tickets and NPS comments. The PM who used to triage it has left, and the team plans the next quarter on Monday. Group the feedback into themes, set the noise aside, flag anything critical, rank the themes by what matters, and write opportunities for the top ones.

themes.label: Customers see other companies' data
themes.summary: A caching change serves some workspaces data from other workspaces. It is a data breach: confidential client work is exposed, with legal and contractual consequences.
themes.opportunity: How might we make it impossible for one workspace to see another's data, starting with turning off the cache and telling affected customers?

themes.label: People cannot log in
themes.summary: Password resets, verification codes and social sign-in fail, and people are locked out of their own data. Every one of these users is fully blocked.
themes.opportunity: How might we make sure nobody stays locked out of Taskhive, with sign-in and recovery that work on the first try?

themes.label: The app got slow
themes.summary: Load times and responsiveness got worse over recent releases. It annoys everyone a little and pushes some people away, but nobody is blocked.
themes.opportunity: How might we make opening Taskhive and loading tasks feel instant again, with a load-time budget every release has to meet?

themes.label: Support is slow
themes.summary: Slow or unhelpful support. It multiplies the pain of every other problem, but it is a symptom as much as a cause.
themes.opportunity: How might we answer the most common questions before people need to contact us, and reply to the rest within a day?

themes.label: Getting started is confusing
themes.summary: New users struggle with the first steps. It costs activation quietly: these people rarely complain twice, they just leave.
themes.opportunity: How might we get a new user to assign a task in their first two minutes, without a tutorial?

themes.label: Too many notifications
themes.summary: Push and email volume annoys people. Easy to fix and worth fixing, but it does not stop anyone from using the product.
themes.opportunity: How might we let people choose which notifications they get, and send fewer that matter more?

themes.label: Requests for a Gantt view
themes.summary: A popular request. It signals what people want next, but its absence does not hurt anyone today.
themes.opportunity: How might we find out which job a Gantt view would do for people, and whether a smaller version solves it?

hidden.explanation: The critical problem, "Customers see other companies' data", appears in only 4 items, all from the last 6 days. Few items, but each describes harm that grows every day it stays live, so it goes first whatever the volume. Volume alone would put "The app got slow" next, with 13 items, but it is a medium-severity problem. "People cannot log in" (9 items, high severity) and "The app got slow" (13 items, medium severity) hurt more people more. Impact here is reach times severity: low counts 1, medium 2, high 3 per item. 8 items were noise: praise, spam and off-topic messages that belong in no theme.
hidden.principle: Rank feedback by reach times severity, not by volume, and read the rare, recent and severe items first: a critical problem is usually quiet before it gets loud.
